facts.raw_span: A woman in her 50s with a history of recent hospitalization for congestive heart failure
developed a painful ulceration on the right distal forearm at a previous peripheral intravenous catheter site
The ulceration appeared a few days after discharge
cleaning her fish tank, playing with her pet cat, and gardening in her indoor cactus garden
No recent travel history or immunosuppressive medications were reported
The patient was readmitted for bacterial pneumonia
ulcerated plaque on the right forearm with 2 tender, 1- to 2-cm red nodules in the right antecubital fossa
marked superficial and deep inflammation composed predominantly of neutrophils with associated tissue necrosis
Multiple filamentous gram-positive bacilli identified on Gram stain
Ziehl Nielson, Fite, and periodic acid–Schiff stains were negative for organisms
Tissue culture: Positive for specific organism

concepts.why: The presence of filamentous gram-positive bacilli on Gram stain and a positive tissue culture for a specific organism are consistent with Nocardia infection.
The development of a painful ulceration at a previous intravenous catheter site, along with the presence of filamentous gram-positive bacilli, supports a diagnosis of cutaneous nocardiosis.
The patient's history of gardening and the presence of a painful ulceration with tender nodules and superficial and deep inflammation are consistent with actinomycetoma.
The patient was readmitted for bacterial pneumonia, which is a separate condition from the skin infection.

rationales.F02: Ulceration at a previous intravenous catheter site is a common presentation for cutaneous nocardiosis
rationales.F04: Exposure to soil or water through gardening or cleaning a fish tank is a risk factor for Nocardia infection
rationales.F06: Bacterial pneumonia is a known complication of Nocardia infection, but in this case, it is a separate diagnosis
rationales.F07: The presence of an ulcerated plaque with red nodules is consistent with cutaneous nocardiosis
rationales.F08: The histopathologic findings of superficial and deep inflammation with tissue necrosis are consistent with Nocardia infection
rationales.F09: The identification of filamentous gram-positive bacilli on Gram stain is highly suggestive of Nocardia infection
rationales.F11: The positive tissue culture for a specific organism, likely Nocardia, confirms the diagnosis
